name: Rails gains a none tier: probe legs run inside the orchestrator with no model (ruling 2)
acceptance: python -m pytest tests/test_rails_none_tier.py harness/jev/tests/test_jev_guards.py -q -p no:cacheprovider exits 0 with at least 5 tests in the new file
python -c "import json;t=json.load(open('harness/rails_exec.json'))['tiers'];assert 'none' in t and t['none'].get('routable') is False" exits 0
grep -n "'none'" harness/orchestrate.ps1 harness/battleplan/compile_wave.py returns at least one line each
python harness/jev/jev_route.py --wave bp4 --shadow output never lists none as a Jev choice
crucible_criteria: a literal tier other than none compiles byte-identical to before
the receipt parser is pure python and tested
the ps1 change is guarded so a missing probe_cmd fails the leg, never spawns claude
note: Add a tier named 'none' to harness/rails_exec.json with a 'why' that says it launches no model. harness/battleplan/mission_schema.py must accept tier 'none' and, for such a mission, require a 'probe_cmd' string (the command the orchestrator runs). harness/battleplan/compile_wave.py must pass tier none and probe_cmd through to the row untouched (a literal tier is byte-identical, per JEV invariant 2; ROUTE must never choose 'none': keep it out of the Choice criteria the route guard builds from rails by giving it 'routable': false and honouring that flag in harness/jev/jev_route._tier_descriptions). harness/orchestrate.ps1: where a leg is launched, if the row's tier is 'none', run probe_cmd via the shell with a timeout, capture stdout and stderr and the exit code into the leg's receipt file (same receipt shape the SCREEN guard reads: status pass/fail from exit code, acceptance rows from lines matching 'ACCEPT: <predicate> :: <pass|fail> :: <evidence>' in stdout, findings from stderr), and mark the leg done; never spawn claude for it. Tests: tests/test_rails_none_tier.py: schema accepts tier none only with probe_cmd; compile_wave passes it through byte-identical; jev_route's tier criteria exclude 'none'; a fake probe command producing two ACCEPT lines yields a receipt with two acceptance rows (drive the receipt parser as a python function you factor out of the ps1 into harness/battleplan/probe_receipt.py so it is testable, and call it from the ps1).

name: Stop and TaskCompleted hooks exit 2 on an unresolved cook error, and the codebase-transition skill exists (ruling 4)
acceptance: python -m pytest tests/test_hooks_stop_gate.py tests/test_hooks_guard_edit.py -q -p no:cacheprovider exits 0 with at least 4 tests in the new file
grep -n 'sys.exit(2)' .claude/hooks/synapse_hooks_bridge.py returns at least one line inside the Stop/TaskCompleted branch
test -f .claude/skills/codebase-transition/SKILL.md and the file has frontmatter with name: codebase-transition
crucible_criteria: exit 2 only on Stop/TaskCompleted with a non-empty unresolved set
missing events file is exit 0, never a false block
the skill text traces to the global CLAUDE.md sections, no invented protocol
hook stays under 100 ms on the no-error path
note: Two changes. (1) .claude/hooks/synapse_hooks_bridge.py: replace the consume-on-prompt watermark for CookError with an 'unresolved' set persisted beside the events file (JSON, one entry per cook error with node path and message, cleared when a later event for the same node reports a successful cook or when the artist prompt contains an explicit 'resolved' marker); on the Stop and TaskCompleted events, if the unresolved set is non-empty, print the one-line list to stderr and exit 2 (the blocking code) instead of exit 1; every other event keeps its current exit code. Keep the hook fast (<= 100 ms) and fail-open ONLY when the events file cannot be read (a missing file means no cook errors, exit 0). This leg starts AFTER BP9-HOOKS merged or from its branch: check git log for a commit mentioning BP9-HOOKS and, if the _ledger.py helper exists, record each fire through it. (2) Write ~/.claude/skills/codebase-transition/SKILL.md (outside the repo; the global CLAUDE.md names it on nine lines and nothing installs it). Frontmatter: name codebase-transition, description covering the triggers (new repo, install or setup language, .md blueprints, moving work to Claude Code, Desktop-to-Code handoff). Body, in the CLAUDE.md house style: the startup-cost ramp (announce the ramp, no steps until orientation), 'you are here' markers with directory, file, step X of Y, handoff formatting for Code (double-spaced numbered steps, one concept per step), the transition-moment beat (slow down at altitude plus tool change), post-handoff silence. Source the wording from the global CLAUDE.md sections 'Transitions', 'Altitude System' and 'Stuck Taxonomy' (read C:/Users/User/.claude/CLAUDE.md); do not invent behaviour it does not describe. Also copy the skill into the repo at .claude/skills/codebase-transition/SKILL.md so the repo carries it. Tests: tests/test_hooks_stop_gate.py drives the bridge hook as a subprocess with a crafted events file: unresolved cook error + Stop event -> exit 2 and stderr names the node; resolved -> exit 0; missing events file -> exit 0; UserPromptSubmit never exits 2.

name: The 70M wave cap is enforced cost-weighted; the ledger shows raw fields, rails total, cost-weighted total and max_ctx (ruling 5)
acceptance: python -m pytest tests/test_cap_cost_basis.py harness/jev/tests/test_jev_guards.py -q -p no:cacheprovider exits 0 with at least 4 tests in the new file
grep -n 'cost_weighted' harness/battleplan/meter_transcript.py harness/battleplan/rails.py returns at least one line each
grep -n 'input_tokens' harness/jev/jev_client.py returns at least one line
crucible_criteria: rails total unchanged for BP8 (regression pin)
cap enforced on cost_weighted, proven by a test that would halt on rails and not on cost
jev ledger rows carry usage without breaking existing tests
note: harness/battleplan/meter_transcript.py currently sums usage with cache reads at 1x. Change it to return the four raw fields (input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, output_tokens), the rails total (all at 1x, unchanged, kept for comparison), a cost_weighted total using weights from a new table in harness/rails_exec.json under 'cost_weights' (default input 1.0, cache_create 1.25, cache_read 0.1, output 5.0) and max_ctx (the largest single-call input including cache fields). harness/battleplan/rails.py (or wherever the 70M ceiling is compared) enforces the cap on cost_weighted; the orch ledger row (see harness/battleplan/runs/2026-09-20/ledger_orch_*.json for the shape) gains the new fields; any dashboard that prints the total prints both totals labelled. harness/jev/jev_client.ask records prompt token count into its ledger row when the SDK response exposes usage (resp.usage.input_tokens per the TypeSafe SDK; None stays None). Tests: tests/test_cap_cost_basis.py replays the three BP8 transcripts if present under harness/battleplan/runs/2026-09-20/ (skip with a reason if absent) and asserts rails total 79.8M plus or minus 1 percent and cost_weighted between 10M and 14M; a synthetic transcript with known counts asserts the exact weighted arithmetic; the cap check halts at 70M cost-weighted and not at 70M rails.
